name: APNs delivery: payload, priority, expiration, collapse
plain: Apple's push channel: 4 KB payload (5 KB VoIP), priority 10 or 5, optional expiry and collapse id.
meaning: Apple holds only the latest push per collapse id and can drop or delay low priority ones. The company learns delivery only as best effort, so apps pair pushes with a fetch on open.

android.note: Android equivalent is FCM; see mob.notif.fcm-delivery

ios.prompt_ui: Alert permission prompt for visible notifications
ios.persistence: Stored up to 30 days when apns-expiration is omitted; 0 means one delivery attempt; only the newest notification per collapse id is kept
ios.store_policy: App Review 4.5.4; APNs token auth key or certificate
ios.note: Payload 4096 bytes (5120 for VoIP), uncompressed JSON; apns-collapse-id max 64 bytes; apns-priority 10 immediate, 5 power considerate, 1 never wakes the device; keep HTTP/2 connections open for hours to days

limits.headline: Can send alerts to an iPhone through Apple, up to 4 KB of data per message
limits.user_action: You allow notifications when the app asks, or you sign in so it can reach your device
can: Send an alert, banner, sound or badge update to your iPhone
Mark a message as urgent or low priority so it is delivered right away or later
Replace an older message with a newer one, and let a message expire if you were offline
cannot: Send a visible alert if you said Don't Allow
Send more than about 4 KB per message, or 5 KB for call pushes
Make a message arrive faster than Apple allows; low priority pushes can wait
Use this on Android, which has its own system
limits.reach_label: Ongoing, whenever the app's server sends
limits.differs: Apple's system is APNs. Android uses Google's FCM instead.

story.what_it_is: Apple's push system that carries small alerts from an app's server to your iPhone.

marketing.name: Apple Push Notification service
marketing.pitch: Apple describes APNs as the service that securely delivers remote notifications from developers' servers to devices.

story.for_you: You see the alert pop up. Behind the scenes, Apple holds the message, may delay low urgency ones, and keeps only the newest version of a repeated alert.
story.for_makers: Makers use it for messages, delivery and news alerts. Because delivery is best effort, they never rely on one push alone and refetch the real data when the app opens.

use_cases.example: A chat app sends a tiny alert so your friend's message shows instantly on the lock screen.
A courier app sends your package is arriving with high priority.
A news app sends breaking news and collapses older alerts so you only see the newest.
A game sends your base is under attack to your phone while the app is closed.
A bank sends a card was used alert, with a short expiry so it is not late.
A retailer sends a flash sale alert and counts who opened it as a measure of the campaign.
A sports app sends goal alerts to fans, with a one time key so duplicates are merged.

story.ios_note: Alerts need your permission. Messages are small, around 4 KB.

technical_bounds: Force quit by the user stops background content pushes until relaunch

abuse: Spam; apps tracking opens via pushes
